inventory_reconciliation.value: Course search reports 239 results; parsed metadata has 238 official pages, with one Science Media Production capture error outside this scope. It contains 23 Business School pages and 45 Medicine pages (68 scoped course-search pages): 67 external candidate-facing course options and one intercalated PhD option restricted to enrolled MBBS students. The 67 external search options comprise 23 Business School plus 44 Medicine options. Add one external Intercalated BSc programme outside course search for 68 candidate-facing routes total; its Faculty page enumerates 16 pathways including Management while the Business School page states 17.

Full-Time MBA, Executive MBA, Global Online MBA, and Weekend MBA are four distinct degree programs, each with its own page and application process; course mode, start and application rounds vary. Business MRes is separately a two-year taught MRes; its joint 2YFT MRes-to-PhD procedure and 3-4-year doctoral progression are parent-owned and must not be represented as an external direct-entry PhD in this file.

Imperial Executive Education and open-enrolment/CPD items are professional short courses, not direct degree routes. The official Executive and Professional Education overview labels Executive Education as short, non-degree provision; the FAQ lists 2–12 day courses and no degree-qualification process. The four MBA routes and external one-year intercalated BSc pathways are degree-awarding and separately inventoried. Business MRes remains the taught MRes route; its doctoral progression procedure is parent-owned. Business School undergraduate catalogue also lists the external one-year Intercalated BSc in Management (a Faculty of Medicine-managed pathway; the Faculty page lists 16 including Management while the Business School states 17), Joint Honours restricted to current Imperial science students, BPES optional modules, and Biomedical Technology Ventures jointly delivered with Bioengineering. Biomedical Technology Ventures is already in the search snapshot and belongs to engineering/natural sciences; it is not a missing-search route. The reviewed apprenticeship inventory lists Levels 3, 4 and 5 with organisation-led enrolment; it did not list a Level 6/7 Business School degree apprenticeship.

Each award level is a separate application only when the official page says it has its own/separate entry point. Exit awards are not routes; online MPH PGDip is an exit award, Digital Health MSc follows the sponsored PGDip, and Business Analytics PGCert/PGDip are exit awards. Award-level options below distinguish explicit entry points, shared master duration pathways, exit/progression awards and unresolved official award conflicts; they supplement the search inventory without duplicating its records.

value.career_outcomes: How will studying at Imperial help my career? Learn from an insider's perspective and gain a wealth of industry knowledge to help you succeed in your career as a climate change expert. Through a partnership with Grantham Institute, we enhance our excellent reputation as a provider of sustainable business education. With its Climate Leadership Award, the programme has been recognized for its innovative approach to addressing the climate crisis. With specialised knowledge, you'll be highly sought after in a range of sectors. Finance, consulting, and CleanTech are just some of your options. Other potential career paths include education and energy.

value.career_outcomes: How will studying at Imperial help my career? Designed specifically for future leaders, Imperial's Executive MBA program offers the first blended MBA in the UK. MBA graduates at Imperial are highly sought after in a variety of employment sectors. Alumni can be found working across sectors as varied as transportation, banking, education and finance. Other potential career paths include communications, social media, design, and defence.
value.course_specific_assessment_publication_s: Course-specific MBA test and selection conditions checked against the dedicated Imperial Business School admissions page.

mba_admission_details.tests: GMAT/GRE is not required. Applicants may provide an existing or new score; a good score can strengthen an application, especially if degree performance does not show academic potential.
mba_admission_details.experience: Normally ten years of relevant postgraduate work experience; candidates with over eight years may be exceptionally considered. Significant management experience is typically five years and may be line, project or matrix management. Academic route: UK 2:2 or international equivalent, or acceptable professional qualification.
mba_admission_details.documents: Online application; current CV, personal statement, full degree transcripts (English translation if needed), two professional referee contact details using business emails, three programme essays, and English scores if required. £150 processing fee; referees are notified after submission.
mba_admission_details.interview: Shortlisted candidates complete an online interview of approximately one hour; date and time are sent by email. Successful applicants are invited to MBA Admit Weekend in London.

english_requirement.qualifying_English_degree_exception: Applicants whose degree was awarded in a qualifying English-speaking country do not need to demonstrate proficiency with a test; all other applicants must meet the approved level.

About TMUA The TMUA is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which tests your mathematical thinking and reasoning skills.
Test dates There will are two test sitting windows for the TMUA for 2027 entry.

For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 15 –1 6 October 2026 Test window 2 : 8 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October TMUA test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to book a test The TMUA is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) .
When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose TMUA , your test date and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee.
More information Find out more about the TMUA , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare.

Check the entry requirements section on this page to learn more about the TMUA and how to register for this test. Selection Assessing your application Admissions Tutors consider all the evidence available during our rigorous selection process and the College flags key information providing assessors with a more complete picture of the educational and social circumstances relevant to the applicant. Some applicants may be set lower offers and some more challenging ones. Interview Post-application interview Successful candidates will be invited to an online interview with an academic (20-30 minutes). The purpose of the interview is for us to find out more about your motivation, analytical thinking, and communication skills. As such, no particular preparation is needed and we do not expect you to demonstrate prior knowledge of economics, finance and/or data science. Our aim, at the meeting, is to identify prospective students who are most likely to enjoy and succeed on the degree.

course_page_summary.Programme content and career: Four-year graduate MBBS at the University of Cumbria Fusehill Street campus in Carlisle, with placements across North and South Cumbria, medical-science and clinical-skills teaching, a community-based prevention/healthcare-delivery project, clinical placements in years 3–4, pre-foundation assistantship and elective. Graduates obtain an Imperial MBBS primary medical qualification and can apply for UK Foundation Year 1; full GMC registration requires Foundation Year 1 completion and application.
course_page_summary.Accommodation and location: First-year accommodation is guaranteed for applicants who make PCSM their first UCAS choice and submit a University of Cumbria accommodation application by 30 June; years 2–4 subject to availability and application by 30 June. Clinical placements can require travel and/or temporary accommodation.
course_page_summary.Degree subject examples and advice: Published UK subject examples include anatomy, biochemistry, bioengineering, biology, biomedical/healthcare science, cell or molecular biology, clinical sciences, dietetics/nutrition, dentistry, genetics, health and social care, medical sciences, microbiology, midwifery, neuroscience, nursing, physiotherapy, paramedic practice/science, pharmacy, pharmacology, physiology, psychology, public health, radiography, sports science/rehabilitation, occupational therapy/health, and veterinary science/medicine. The list is non-exhaustive; applicants with an unlisted degree or a degree awarded outside the UK are told to contact Cumbria Med Admissions to check suitability.

The UCAT You will need to take the University Clinical Aptitude Test (UCAT) to study this course.
Find out more about the UCAT and how to register.
How we use the UCAT The School of Medicine will initially review applications to ensure they meet our minimum academic entry requirements as outlined in our Study pages.
Following receipt of UCAT scores in November, we then begin inviting candidates to attend our Multiple Mini Interviews (MMIs).
Each year, we normally interview the top 1/3 of applicants and will send invitations on a rolling basis from December.
Invitations will explain in detail how the interview will work.
For 2027 entry, all candidates who submitted special circumstances via UCAT will be examined carefully on a case-by-case basis.
We are unable to consider any mitigating circumstances that do not come via UCAT directly.
UCAT scores are used to help decide shortlisting for interview but are not the sole factor.

For 2026 entry, the following UCAT thresholds were applied: UCAT Threshold for Home Applicants SJT: Band 3 minimum (Band 4 discounted) Minimum threshold Total Score: 2320 UCAT Thresholds for Contextual Applicants SJT: Band 3 minimum (Band 4 discounted) Minimum threshold total Score: 2170 All candidates who attend the test are declaring that they are fit to sit the test.
If circumstances occur which might affect performance, candidates must refer to the UCAT Fitness to Test Policy before sitting their test.
On occasion the UCAT Office may communicate significant personal/medical circumstances to the medical school.

course_specific_application_materials: No offers are made without applicants attending a competitive interview.

The following criteria may be considered when assessing your application: A-level or equivalent predicted (or achieved) grades UCAT scores Referee’s report Personal statement Fitness to Practise policy All UK medical schools have a duty to ensure that no member of the public is harmed as a consequence of training medical students.
Interview If you are shortlisted, you will be invited to take part in Multiple Mini Interviews (MMIs).
The interviews are conducted by a combination of academic staff involved in undergraduate education and experienced healthcare professionals.

The following criteria may be considered when we assess you: evidence of commitment to the values of the NHS Constitution motivation and understanding of medicine as a career empathy work experience and community activities leadership and teamwork Your personal statement may be referred to during the interview stage.
Find out more about our interview process .
Special arrangements for interviews If you are invited to interview, you can request special arrangements to help make sure you can attend.
Please inform us on special adjustments via the survey when you are invited to interview.

Mitigating circumstances If you want us to consider Mitigating Circumstances during the admissions cycle, please refer to the forms below: Mitigating Circumstances Form for MMIs (Deadline 5 working days before your interview) : use this form if you feel you have mitigating circumstances that should be taken into consideration during your Multiple Mini Interviews.
You must state in your UCAS personal statement how you propose to spend your time.
If you wish to make a deferral request in cycle, it is essential that you apply as soon as possible to FEO Admissions Interviews feo-admissions-interviews@imperial.ac.uk .

value.application_deadline_and_schedule: Application deadlines – Thursday 15 October 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Admissions test – the UCAT You will need to take the University Clinical Aptitude Test (UCAT) to study this course. You must book the test yourself and must only take it once in an admissions cycle. It must be taken in the year that you apply. See the University Clinical Aptitude Test website for registration and test dates. We encourage you to book your test slot at local centre as soon as registration opens. For more information on how we use the UCAT as part of the admissions process, please refer to the entry requirements section of this page. Selection Assessing your application Admission to medicine at Imperial is highly competitive. We use a range of criteria to assess candidates. You must meet the minimum academic requirements and have taken the UCAT admissions test. No offers are made without applicants attending a competitive interview. The following criteria may be considered when assessing your application: A-level or equivalent predicted (or achieved) grades UCAT scores Referee’s report Personal statement Fitness to Practise policy All UK medical schools have a duty to ensure that no member of the public is harmed as a consequence of training medical students. The School of Medicine’s Fitness to Practise policy (PDF) may be activated in cases where significant concerns have been raised about the behaviour of students, including prior to their admission to the School. Interview If you are shortlisted, you will be invited to take part in Multiple Mini Interviews (MMIs). The interviews are conducted by a combination of academic staff involved in undergraduate education and experienced healthcare professionals. The following criteria may be considered when we assess you: evidence of commitment to the values of the NHS Constitution motivation and understanding of medicine as a career empathy work experience and community activities leadership and teamwork Your personal statement may be referred to during the interview stage. Find out more about our interview process . Special arrangements for interviews If you are invited to interview, you can request special arrangements to help make sure you can attend. For example, you may have existing exam arrangements, have unique personal circumstances, or are undertaking military service. Please inform us on special adjustments via the survey

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: You will study all these core modules.

Build essential skills in law, programming, and economics as a foundation for advanced study. published_requirement_or_structure_notes: You will take six to seven electives throughout the year depending on the credit value of the modules selected.

Electives will allow you to develop specialist knowledge across rapidly evolving fields such as machine learning, natural language processing, formal methods for safe AI, and domain-specific applications. Each elective will introduce the core analytical models, frameworks, and ethical considerations shaping the modern data-driven landscape.

Deliver a substantial, independent AI project that synthesises your learning across the programme. This capstone module develops your ability to research, design, and implement advanced AI solutions, while demonstrating originality, technical skill, and effective communication through a scholarly report and presentation.

Undertake an internship in industry as an alternative to the Individual Project. Apply programme knowledge in a professional setting, work on a substantial real-world problem and develop independence, analytical skills and effective communication through a final report and presentation, with support from both workplace and academic supervisors.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: The Imperial Executive MBA electives allow you to specialise in areas of particular interest, developing your expertise with your future career objectives in mind. Our elective options also feature many modules that are offered online, ideal if you have a less flexible work schedule or commute long distances.
You can choose five electives. Electives run in the spring and summer terms of your second year.
Electives are offered in four formats to fit into your schedule:
We also offer a Final Project as an elective, where you’ll work on a real business problem and demonstrate your decision-making and leadership abilities.

The Final Project is a formal report consisting of up to 15,000 words, completed in the second year of the programme. This elective allows you to address a real business problem – you can focus on an issue facing your current employer or an industry of interest.

In order to make an impact on a global scale, you must understand the global environment in which you are working. As an MBA student, you will have opportunities to travel to international destinations to study at partner schools and work with local businesses.

As part of your elective modules, you will complete three immersions developing your knowledge and understanding of deep tech and entrepreneurship ecosystems. These experiences include enhanced ecosystem exposure while bringing industry in the classroom.

The Capstone module takes place in a European tech hub over a five-day period during your second year and provides a practical, immersive opportunity to apply the knowledge, frameworks, and skills developed throughout the programme.
Working intensively in multi-disciplinary teams, you will be required to draw upon your analytical capabilities, strategic thinking, and ability to operate effectively under time pressure.

Global Experience Week takes place during the summer term. It is an unforgettable opportunity that MBA students eagerly anticipate each year. You will learn about the challenges faced by local organisations. You will also explore how a country’s business environment influences their operations.

The optional Global Exchanges programme allows you to increase your international exposure and connect with a global community. You can also build your network by taking advantage of specialised electives at one of our partner schools.

The year-long Executive Leadership Journey will enhance your awareness of your own and other’s strengths. You will work closely with a Careers consultant throughout the programme. Together, you will develop a plan for your future career trajectory. You will also gain insights into yourself and build essential leadership skills.
